<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אייר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918633_theRebbe_459" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_99_D7_99_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918633_theRebbe_459__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that "Midbar" (desert) is related to speech in a state of self-nullification, and that on Rosh Chodesh Sivan the refinement of the core animal soul traits was completed.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is, "On this day they came to the desert of Sinai,"</t>
    <t s="2">and it is explained in Torah Ohr,</t>
    <t s="3">that "midbar" (desert) is from the term "dibur" (speech),</t>
    <t s="4">and it is called "midbar" with the addition of the letter mem</t>
    <t s="5">(for mem is one of the letters of Emanti"o that indicate a diminishment of the matter26)</t>
    <t s="6">to indicate that the speech is in a state of self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="7">[And this concept also applies to a desert in its simple sense,</t>
    <t s="8">"a land not sown"27,</t>
    <t s="9">for when speech is according to one's intellect and will,</t>
    <t s="10">the intellect and will are the sowing through which the growth of speech occurs.</t>
    <t s="11">And the concept of a desert, a land not sown, is that the speech of Torah that one speaks is the word of G-d and is not sown from his own intellect and will28].</t>
    <t s="12">And "Sinai" is that hatred descended upon the nations of the world29,</t>
    <t s="13">and it is that the Torah is called "Tushiyah"30</t>
    <t s="14">because it weakens the power of the sitra achra.</t>
    <t s="15">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="16">that this that "on this day they came to the desert" is because on this day</t>
    <t s="17">(Rosh Chodesh)</t>
    <t s="18">the moon</t>
    <t s="19">[and likewise Israel who count by the moon]</t>
    <t s="20">is only a point,</t>
    <t s="21">and this that on this day they came to Sinai, that hatred descended upon the evil inclination31,</t>
    <t s="22">is because on this day</t>
    <t s="23">(Rosh Chodesh Sivan)</t>
    <t s="24">the refinement of the core traits of the animal soul was completed.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the self-nullification of Rosh Chodesh is not the nullification of existence, but rather that one's existence itself is in a state of nullification, which connects the moon's renewal with the completion of the traits.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="2">that according to the above,</t>
    <t s="3">this that on Rosh Chodesh Sivan the core traits were completed is an explanation in the perfection of man,</t>
    <t s="4">and in the discourse in Torah Ohr it connects this with that on Rosh Chodesh is the birth of the moon,</t>
    <t s="5">the concept of self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="6">And the explanation of this can be said,</t>
    <t s="7">that the concept of the birth of the moon is</t>
    <t s="8">(not its self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="9">but rather on the contrary32)</t>
    <t s="10">that its existence is born,</t>
    <t s="11">by the light of the sun being drawn into it.</t>
    <t s="12">And this that at the time of its birth it is only a point,</t>
    <t s="13">which indicates its self-nullification</t>
    <t s="14">(as above),</t>
    <t s="15">is,</t>
    <t s="16">that the existence of the moon,</t>
    <t s="17">its light,</t>
    <t s="18">is in a state of self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="19">so that it is felt that the light within it is not from itself and it only receives from the sun.</t>
    <t s="20">And likewise is it with Israel who count by the moon,</t>
    <t s="21">that the concept of the self-nullification of Rosh Chodesh in the service of man is that his existence is in a state of self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="22">[And it can be said that this is what is explained in Torah Ohr, that this that Rosh Chodesh is called "this day"</t>
    <t s="23">(without specification)</t>
    <t s="24">is because "this day" is love that is in the aspect of self-nullification</t>
    <t s="25">[for "day" is light, as it is written33</t>
    <t s="26">"And G-d called the light day," and love is light,</t>
    <t s="27">and this is yichudah ila'ah</t>
    <t s="28">(therefore Moshe Rabbeinu prophesied with this34),</t>
    <t s="29">and "this day" is love that is in the aspect of self-nullification of yichudah ila'ah],</t>
    <t s="30">for one of the reasons that love is called by the name "light,"</t>
    <t s="31">is,</t>
    <t s="32">because love is an expansion35</t>
    <t s="33">[and therefore fear, which is a contraction</t>
    <t s="34">(the opposite of expansion)</t>
    <t s="35">is called by the name "darkness"36],</t>
    <t s="36">and the self-nullification of Rosh Chodesh is not in a manner that one is nullified from his existence</t>
    <t s="37">(like the self-nullification of fear),</t>
    <t s="38">but rather,</t>
    <t s="39">that the expansion</t>
    <t s="40">(the existence)</t>
    <t s="41">of his is in a state of self-nullification].</t>
    <t s="42">And based on this, the connection of the two concepts of Rosh Chodesh Sivan can be explained</t>
    <t s="43">(the self-nullification of the moon and the completion of the core traits),</t>
    <t s="44">for the concept of the birth of the moon is that the existence is in a state of self-nullification.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the self-nullification of "Midbar" is a nullification of existence itself, which is a higher level than the self-nullification of "this day," yet the lesson from "this day" points to an even higher level.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this, it can be explained what the Tosafos questioned, that it should have learned "midbar" from "midbar,"</t>
    <t s="2">for this that on Rosh Chodesh Sivan they came to the aspect of "midbar" is a self-nullification more elevated than that Rosh Chodesh is called "this day."</t>
    <t s="3">For the concept of "this day" is that it has existence</t>
    <t s="4">(even to the extent of the existence of expansion,</t>
    <t s="5">"day")</t>
    <t s="6">except that its existence is in a state of self-nullification</t>
    <t s="7">("this"),</t>
    <t s="8">but not so this that on Rosh Chodesh Sivan they came to the aspect of "midbar"</t>
    <t s="9">[that his speech is not his own speech at all,</t>
    <t s="10">and here the person is only a vessel for the word of G-d that speaks through him,</t>
    <t s="11">similar to "the word of G-d in the mouth of the prophet"37]</t>
    <t s="12">is a nullification of existence.</t>
    <t s="13">And since the main virtue of Rosh Chodesh Sivan is that on it they came to the self-nullification of "midbar,"</t>
    <t s="14">therefore there is room to say that the hint in the verse</t>
    <t s="15">(that this was on Rosh Chodesh Sivan)</t>
    <t s="16">is in the word "midbar"38.</t>
    <t s="17">And this that the lesson in the Gemara is from "on this day,"</t>
    <t s="18">is,</t>
    <t s="19">for the concept of "this day" of Rosh Chodesh Sivan is more elevated even than the self-nullification of "midbar,"</t>
    <t s="20">as will be explained below.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
